Now, I don't think that it's worth our while exploring the exact geographical location of those killings. And I think all I have to do is give a description which locates them sufficiently. And that's all that I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And if I may add, unless I misunderstood Mr. Krgovic, the issue is the amendment of the indictment, not the quality of the evidence in support of the charge, so it's ... So leave to amend the indictment, as prayed, is granted. And -- leave to amend the indictment is granted as prayed, if I might correct myself. And we require the Prosecution, for tidiness, to file a corrected indictment accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can it just be a correct -- Your Honours, rather than the whole indictment, just the corrected schedule to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: A correction reflecting the amendment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, it has been pointed out to me to answer Judge Delvoie's question about Banja Luka and Sanski Most, and I will do it now so you can get some idea, although I'll double-check it, is that that relates to the victims who were suffocated outside Manjaca camp which is in the Banja Luka municipality but their bodies were actually exhumed in Sanski Most. So it's under the overall title "Banja Luka." But the bodies, because it's the Manjaca camp, were actually exhumed in Sanski Most. And that, I'm told, is the explanation of that. I'll have to check on the Skender Vakuf. But I have a feeling -- or, rather, we think that those are recent exhumations which have been taking place in Skender Vakuf. And they are in fact the bodies, very recently, indeed, the bodies of those who were killed at the Koricanske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Then I have perhaps two other clarification question, Ms. Korner. There are three incident codes -- no, no -- that's an easy one. That's -- I don't need to bother you with that. But there are quite some victims that are not linked to an incident in the indictment. What is your view on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could Your Honour perhaps give me an example and I'll see if my ever-hard-working juniors behind me will give me the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner, I could give you 1.425 examples. There are -- you have -- have you the column of the incident code.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: In -- for 1.425 victims, victims' names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The incident code cell is blank. There is no incident code. And the incident code is what links the victim to a certain incident in the indictment. For example, 6.1 is Koricanske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So what about the 1.425 that have no incident code?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just don't know at the moment, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I really -- I think I'll -- I need to speak to Ms. Kipp about all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And what strikes me is -- oh, no. No. The majority of them are -- not the majority. All of them, except one, are new victims. So new victims without incident code.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will certainly get back to Your Honours on -- on that as soon as I've got an answer. Your Honours, would it perhaps -- would Your Honours agree to this. I don't know if Your Honours want to sit again this week. But we could provide the answers via e-mail, copied to the Defence, to the Legal Officer to the questions Your Honour has just asked. But, I mean, if Your Honours wasn't to sit, then I can certainly deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we were thinking that there may be a possibility that we would have to -- having regard to the matter of the -- when we would have had -- when the Chamber would have had the opportunity to consider the material which the OTP has been directed to provide by the end of today, when we would have analyzed it, there may be a possibility - you would be notified by e-mail in the course of tomorrow - but there may be a possibility that we would reconvene on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On Friday. Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Friday, on Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Your Honours invited us to give or position on the motion of the 13th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- of February considering denying protective measures to two witnesses. Well, Your Honours, I can inform you that the position of the -- both Defences is that we take no position on that -- on that motion of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And there is one additional matter. I would respectfully need to ask Your Honours to rule today on our motion for extension of -- of time. Because, Your Honours, we asked for the -- for the extension to respond to the bar table motion. And, unfortunately, the deadline for response is tomorrow, so we would need to know what is the -- I mean, we know that the Office of the Prosecutor took no position on that, but we don't know what the -- the decision of the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Chamber, having considered the application by the Defence for an extension of time, agrees to the motion in part and grants an extension to Wednesday, the 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just go back, for a moment, to amending the indictment. It's been pointed out to me that as we don't yet know whether there's going to be a Rule 98 bis submission and we don't know yet whether that may have an effect on the indictment, could we leave the formal amending -- written amendment until after the 98 bis? I mean, everybody knows it's there. Because if we have to amend the indictment as a result of any rulings then, we have yet another amended version. So perhaps we could just save that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Unless I'm persuaded otherwise, it seems eminently sensible, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Provided that, of course, the OTP flags this as a matter with which they have to deal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. No, no, we've got this flagged, Your Honour, and we'll make sure that it's there after the Rule 98 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So I believe that brings us to the end of the matters with which we had to deal today. And as I indicated to Ms. Korner, we adjourn with the possibility ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Parties should also expect to receive from the Chamber by tomorrow a Scheduling Order. The -- to set out the time-periods within which the remainder of the trial, more specifically the case for the Defence, or the progress of the trial pending the -- following the close of the case of the Prosecution, would be expected to follow. The -- it may be necessary, as I indicated earlier, to reconvene on Friday morning, after the Chamber would have had a chance to consider the material that the Prosecution has been directed to supply by this afternoon. And if that should occur, the parties will be notified in the usual manner by e-mail in the course of tomorrow. Failing that, we would reconvene at the conclusion of the winter recess. And the last version of the calendar I saw is that we're sitting on the afternoon of the 10th. But, of course, persons know that the calendar is subject to change, particularly so far in advance. So should we not reconvene on Friday, I take the opportunity to wish that everyone has a safe and happy holiday and that we all return refreshed for a productive new year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, if I may just -- one question. Your Honours, I believe the arrangements for the travel of Mr. Stanisic on provisional release have been made for Friday, and there is -- there is -- there is a certain procedure, as you know, that the officer needs to fly in here and take him at the airport. So if it would be possible that Mr. Stanisic, if we are sitting on Friday, that Mr. Stanisic waive his presence for that Status Conference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so we take that as an application that his presence be waived, and it is, of course, granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.
